questions.stem: What does API / Service Data Modelling concentrate on?
options: How data is exposed, requested and consumed across interfaces
How data is physically stored in tables
How data is partitioned across cluster nodes
How data is normalised to remove redundancy
How events are replayed to rebuild state
questions.explanation: Rather than focusing on internal storage, API / Service Data Modelling designs the data contracts that define how information is exchanged between services, applications and systems.

questions.stem: In API / Service Data Modelling, what role does a well-designed API model play between systems?
options: A caching layer
A formal contract between service providers and service consumers
A replacement for the database schema
A physical index
An event log
questions.explanation: API models act as formal contracts between providers and consumers, reducing integration complexity, preventing misunderstandings and minimising runtime errors.

questions.stem: Which standards are named for expressing API data models?
options: SQL DDL, ERD and UML
JSON Schema, XSD and DTD
OpenAPI (Swagger) for REST, GraphQL schemas and WSDL for SOAP
OWL, RDF and SPARQL
Avro, Parquet and ORC
questions.explanation: API data models are typically expressed using OpenAPI (Swagger) for REST services, GraphQL schemas for flexible querying or WSDL for SOAP-based services.

questions.stem: In the loan approval API ecosystem, which endpoint do regulatory authorities consume for compliance monitoring?
options: /loanApplications
/loanApprovals
/loanOfficers
/loanReports
/customers
questions.explanation: The mobile app calls /loanApplications, underwriting uses /loanApprovals and regulators consume /loanReports for compliance monitoring.

questions.stem: What happens to the API schema if a bank's internal storage shifts from relational databases to NoSQL or event-driven architectures?
options: It must be rewritten for every consumer
It becomes a GraphQL schema automatically
It is replaced by direct database access
It is versioned as a new major release
It remains stable, ensuring consistent communication across stakeholders
questions.explanation: The API schema decouples internal database structures from external consumers, so backend changes do not break integrations.

questions.stem: What advantage does the GraphQL loan example illustrate?
options: A consumer can request only specific fields such as LoanAmount, Status and the related names, avoiding unnecessary data transfer
A consumer receives every field of every related entity in one call
A consumer can update the database schema directly
A consumer can bypass the API contract
A consumer can submit XML instead of JSON
questions.explanation: In a GraphQL model the consumer requests only the fields it needs, such as LoanAmount, Status and the Customer and Officer names.

questions.stem: Which fields does the REST request to POST /loanApplications contain in the loan approval example?
options: LoanID, Status and InterestRate
CustomerID, LoanAmount and OfficerID
LoanID, ApprovalStatus and Term
OfficerID, Branch and Region
CustomerID, Name and CreditScore
questions.explanation: The example request payload contains CustomerID, LoanAmount and OfficerID; the response returns LoanID, Status and nested Officer and Customer details.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a challenge of API / Service Data Modelling?
options: Over-fetching or under-fetching of data in REST APIs
Versioning and backward compatibility requiring careful governance
Inability to represent nested objects
Exposing too much internal detail
Providing insufficient context for consumers
questions.explanation: API payloads readily carry nested object-like structures; the named challenges are over- and under-fetching, versioning governance and poorly balanced exposure of detail.

questions.stem: Why do normalisation forms not apply to API modelling?
options: Because APIs store data in 6NF by default
Because APIs use only flat structures
Because APIs cannot carry keys
Because the focus is message exchange, where canonical representations matter more than normalised schemas
Because APIs are always backed by NoSQL
questions.explanation: The key concern in API modelling is whether systems agree on the structure and meaning of exchanged data, not relational storage, so canonical representations matter more than normal forms.

questions.stem: How does Object-Oriented Data Modelling differ from API / Service Data Modelling, given that both represent entities as rich nested objects?
options: APIs store methods with the data while OODM does not
OODM uses JSON while APIs use binary formats
APIs are older than OODM
OODM is used only for regulators
OODM bundled logic with data inside the database, whereas APIs keep only the data representation and leave logic in application code or services
questions.explanation: An OODM LoanApplication object maps almost one-to-one to an API response body, but OODM tried to make the database itself object-oriented while APIs separate storage from application logic.
